chapter: Tenor players, tours and band boys
title: Records with Lucky Millinder: Apollo Jump, Shout Sister Shout and others
summary: He names hits with Lucky Millinder and Sister Tharpe, mostly on race labels as two-sided records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Remember some of the things you did with Lucky?
Oh, sure ... I did Sweet Slumber which was a big hit for him, and "When The Lights Go On Again All Over the World."
Oh, that was really a big hit.
That was a world wide hit. During the war.

Yeah, that's right -- during the war. "Big Fat Mama, "Slide Your Horn, Mr. Trombone, "Shipyard Social Function, "Apollo Jump." Now almost all of these records were bit hits, but they were bit hits, like on the Race label; I men, mostly of them among black people, you know?
Yeah, and these were records with two sides. There was no albums -- they were just two sided records.
Yeah, two sided records. Yeah, two sided records. And "Shout Sister Shout."
What we would call a single now.
Yeah, they do-call them singles now --

they were called two-sided records then. We had "Shout Sister Shout, Trouble In Mind, with Sister Thorpe; "Rock, Daniel," which was a big hit for her, and "Let Me Off Uptown," "Savoy," "Little John Special."
Oh, "Little John Special" -- that was a big hit, wasn't it?
Yeah, that was a biggie. "Rock Around the Clock," "Don't Cry Baby," "Ride Red Ride," the second version-- we did the first one with Red Allen with the Mills Blue Rhythm Band.

And then he did a second one with the three trumpets playing all of Red's solos. That is the second version of that. And then we did "The Walk," "Who Threw The Whiskey In the Well?" I did that one with Wymone Harris, which was a big hit.
